tasks.title: Design and Document Core Data Models
tasks.description: Define the foundational data structures for units, attacks, targeting rules, and character sheets with clear documentation
tasks.details: Create TypeScript interfaces/classes for: Unit (base properties like id, name, type), Attack (name, damage calculation, targeting rule), TargetingRule (enum/interface for different targeting patterns), CharacterSheet (base stats like strength, agility), and CombatStats (derived stats like attack, initiative). Document the relationships between these models in code comments or markdown. Use composition over inheritance where possible for extensibility.
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests to validate data model integrity, ensure proper inheritance/composition, and verify that combat stats are correctly derived from character sheet base stats

subtasks.title: Design Unit Model Definition
subtasks.description: Create the foundational Unit model class with core properties, methods, and interfaces that will serve as the base for all game entities
subtasks.details: Define Unit class structure including unique identifiers, name, type classification, position/location properties, state management (active/inactive/destroyed), and base interface methods. Establish inheritance patterns and extensibility points for specialized unit types. Include validation rules and serialization support.

subtasks.title: Implement Attack Model with Damage Calculation Logic
subtasks.description: Design and implement the Attack model containing damage calculation algorithms, attack types, and combat mechanics
subtasks.details: Create Attack class with damage calculation methods, attack type enumeration (physical, magical, ranged, etc.), damage formulas incorporating base damage, modifiers, and random factors. Include critical hit logic, damage resistance calculations, and attack validation. Integrate with Unit model for attack execution.

subtasks.title: Design TargetingRule Interface System
subtasks.description: Create a flexible TargetingRule interface system to handle various targeting mechanics and constraints
subtasks.details: Define TargetingRule interface with methods for target validation, range checking, line-of-sight calculations, and area-of-effect targeting. Implement concrete targeting rule classes for different scenarios (single target, multi-target, friendly fire, etc.). Include targeting priority algorithms and constraint validation.

subtasks.title: Implement CharacterSheet with Base Stats Structure
subtasks.description: Design the CharacterSheet model containing all base character statistics and attribute management
subtasks.details: Create CharacterSheet class with core attributes (strength, dexterity, intelligence, etc.), health/mana pools, level progression system, and stat modification methods. Include stat validation, bounds checking, and persistence mechanisms. Design for extensibility to support different character classes and custom attributes.

subtasks.title: Develop CombatStats Derivation System with Relationships Documentation
subtasks.description: Create the CombatStats system that derives combat-relevant statistics from base stats and documents all model relationships
subtasks.details: Implement CombatStats class that calculates derived statistics (attack power, defense, accuracy, etc.) from CharacterSheet base stats. Create comprehensive documentation of relationships between Unit, Attack, CharacterSheet, and CombatStats models. Include dependency mapping, data flow diagrams, and integration patterns for the complete combat system.

tasks.title: Implement Unit Factory and Registry System
tasks.description: Create a factory pattern for unit creation and a registry system to manage available units and attacks
tasks.details: Implement UnitFactory class with methods like createPlayerUnit(type) and createEnemyUnit(type). Create UnitRegistry to store unit templates and AttackRegistry for attack definitions. Use enum or constants for unit types (BEAR, TIGER, EAGLE, GOOBER). Factory should instantiate units with proper character sheets and attacks based on type. Registry should support easy addition of new unit types without modifying existing code.
tasks.testStrategy: Test factory creation of all unit types, verify registry contains expected units/attacks, ensure factory throws appropriate errors for invalid types, and validate that created units have correct default stats and attacks

subtasks.title: Implement unit type constants and enums with validation logic
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive enums and constants for unit types, attributes, and properties. Include validation methods to ensure data integrity and type safety across the unit system.
subtasks.details: Define UnitType enum, AttributeType enum, unit property constants, and validation functions for unit parameters. Include error handling for invalid unit configurations and type checking utilities.

subtasks.title: Develop AttackRegistry for attack definitions and management
subtasks.description: Create a registry system to store, retrieve, and manage attack definitions including damage types, effects, and attack patterns. Implement methods for attack registration and lookup.
subtasks.details: Build AttackRegistry class with methods for registering attacks, retrieving attack data, validating attack definitions, and managing attack templates. Include support for different damage types and special effects.

subtasks.title: Build UnitRegistry system for storing unit templates
subtasks.description: Implement a registry pattern to store and manage unit templates with efficient lookup and retrieval mechanisms. Include template validation and error handling for missing or invalid templates.
subtasks.details: Create UnitRegistry class with template storage, retrieval methods, template validation, and caching mechanisms. Support for template inheritance and composition patterns.

subtasks.title: Create UnitFactory class with unit creation methods
subtasks.description: Implement the factory pattern for unit creation using registered templates and attack definitions. Include methods for creating units with proper initialization and dependency injection.
subtasks.details: Build UnitFactory class with createUnit methods, template-based instantiation, attack assignment, unit initialization, and error handling for creation failures. Integrate with both registries for complete unit assembly.

tasks.title: Implement Character Sheet System
tasks.description: Build the character sheet system that stores base stats and derives active combat stats for all units
tasks.details: Create CharacterSheet class with base stats (strength, agility, health, etc.). Implement stat derivation logic: attack = strength + weapon_bonus, initiative = agility + speed_bonus, etc. Each unit type should have predefined base stats. Create methods like getAttackStat(), getInitiativeStat(), getHealthStat(). Ensure the system is extensible for future stat additions and modifications.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for stat calculations, verify base stats are correctly set for each unit type, test stat derivation formulas, and ensure character sheet modifications properly update derived combat stats

tasks.title: Implement Core Targeting System
tasks.description: Build the targeting rule engine that determines valid targets for different attack types
tasks.details: Create TargetingEngine class with methods for different targeting patterns: targetInFront(), targetOneRight(), etc. Implement position-based targeting logic considering unit positions on battlefield. Create TargetingRule interface with execute(attacker, battlefield) method. Support for 'no valid target' scenarios. Make system extensible for future targeting patterns like area-of-effect, random target, etc.
tasks.testStrategy: Test each targeting rule with various battlefield configurations, verify correct target selection, test edge cases like no valid targets, and ensure targeting works correctly with different unit positions

subtasks.title: Design TargetingEngine Class Structure
subtasks.description: Create the main TargetingEngine class with core architecture for managing targeting operations, rule registration, and target validation
subtasks.details: Implement TargetingEngine class with methods for rule registration, target calculation, battlefield state management, and coordinate system handling. Include constructor for battlefield dimensions and unit positioning.

subtasks.title: Define TargetingRule Interface
subtasks.description: Create the TargetingRule interface with standardized execution methods for all targeting patterns
subtasks.details: Design interface with methods like execute(), validateTarget(), calculateTargets(), and getTargetPositions(). Include parameters for source position, battlefield state, and targeting constraints.

subtasks.title: Implement Individual Targeting Rule Classes
subtasks.description: Create concrete implementations for directional targeting rules (front, right, left, back, diagonal, etc.)
subtasks.details: Implement FrontTargetingRule, RightTargetingRule, LeftTargetingRule, BackTargetingRule, and DiagonalTargetingRule classes. Each should handle position calculations, range validation, and obstacle detection.

subtasks.title: Develop Position-Based Battlefield Logic
subtasks.description: Implement battlefield coordinate system, position validation, and spatial relationship calculations
subtasks.details: Create BattlefieldGrid class with coordinate mapping, distance calculations, line-of-sight algorithms, and position validation. Include methods for checking valid moves and target accessibility.

subtasks.title: Implement Edge Case Handling and Validation
subtasks.description: Add comprehensive error handling for invalid targets, out-of-bounds positions, and edge battlefield scenarios
subtasks.details: Implement validation for null targets, boundary checking, friendly fire prevention, obstacle collision detection, and invalid rule combinations. Include exception handling and fallback targeting strategies.

tasks.title: Implement Player Units (Bear, Tiger, Eagle)
tasks.description: Create the three player units with their unique attacks and character sheets
tasks.details: Implement Bear unit with Slash attack (targets enemy in front), Tiger with Pounce attack (targets enemy in front), and Eagle with Swoop attack (targets enemy one to the right). Each unit should have distinct base stats in their character sheets. Define attack damage calculations and ensure proper integration with targeting system. Store attack names for UI display.
tasks.testStrategy: Test each unit's attack targeting and damage calculation, verify character sheet stats are correctly applied, test attack execution in various battlefield scenarios, and ensure attack names are properly stored and accessible

tasks.title: Implement Enemy Unit (Goober)
tasks.description: Create the Goober enemy unit with its Slam attack and appropriate stats
tasks.details: Implement Goober enemy unit with Slam attack that targets enemy in front. Define appropriate base stats for enemy balance. Ensure Goober integrates properly with the unit factory and targeting system. Consider enemy-specific behavior patterns if needed for future AI implementation.
tasks.testStrategy: Test Goober creation through factory, verify Slam attack targeting and damage, ensure proper integration with combat system, and test enemy unit behavior in combat scenarios

tasks.title: Implement Combat Logic and Turn Management
tasks.description: Build the core combat engine that manages turn order, attack execution, and missed attack handling
tasks.details: Create CombatEngine class to manage turn-based combat flow. Implement initiative-based turn order using derived stats. Handle attack execution by calling targeting system and applying damage. Implement missed attack logic: when no valid target exists, move to next unit to the left. Manage combat state transitions and victory/defeat conditions.
tasks.testStrategy: Test turn order calculation based on initiative, verify attack execution and damage application, test missed attack handling with various scenarios, and ensure proper combat state management throughout battles

subtasks.title: CombatEngine class structure
subtasks.description: Design and implement the core CombatEngine class with proper initialization, state variables, and method organization for managing combat flow
subtasks.details: Create the main CombatEngine class with constructor, private/public methods for combat orchestration, state management variables, and integration points for other combat systems. Include proper error handling and logging mechanisms.

subtasks.title: Initiative-based turn order calculation
subtasks.description: Implement the initiative system that determines combat turn order based on unit stats and random factors
subtasks.details: Develop algorithm to calculate initiative values for all combat participants, sort units by initiative, handle tie-breaking scenarios, and maintain turn order queue throughout combat rounds.

subtasks.title: Attack execution and damage application logic
subtasks.description: Create the core attack resolution system that processes attacks and applies damage to targets
subtasks.details: Implement hit/miss calculations, damage computation based on attacker/defender stats, critical hit mechanics, damage type considerations, and health reduction with proper validation and bounds checking.

subtasks.title: Missed attack handling with unit repositioning
subtasks.description: Develop system for handling missed attacks including potential unit movement and positioning changes
subtasks.details: Create logic for miss consequences, unit repositioning mechanics when attacks fail, collision detection for movement, and updating unit positions on the battlefield grid while maintaining combat flow.

subtasks.title: Combat state management
subtasks.description: Implement comprehensive combat state tracking and transition management system
subtasks.details: Design state machine for combat phases (initialization, turn execution, resolution), track active effects, manage unit status conditions, handle state persistence, and ensure proper state transitions with validation.

subtasks.title: Victory/defeat condition detection
subtasks.description: Create system to detect and handle combat end conditions including victory, defeat, and draw scenarios
subtasks.details: Implement win/loss condition checking after each action, handle multiple victory conditions (elimination, objectives, time limits), trigger appropriate end-game events, and clean up combat state upon completion.

tasks.title: Implement Run Initialization System
tasks.description: Create the system that initializes each run with Bear, Tiger, and Eagle as the starting team
tasks.details: Implement RunManager or GameInitializer class that creates a new run with the default team composition. Use the unit factory to create Bear, Tiger, and Eagle instances. Set up initial team positioning and ensure proper integration with combat system. Prepare foundation for future team customization features.
tasks.testStrategy: Test run initialization creates correct starting team, verify all three units are properly instantiated with correct stats and attacks, and ensure team is ready for combat engagement

tasks.description: Modify the combat screen UI to show each unit's attack name in their character card stats section
tasks.details: Update character card components to display attack names from unit data. Ensure attack names are fetched from the unit's attack property and displayed in the stats section. Maintain clean separation between UI components and combat logic. Consider responsive design for different screen sizes.

tasks.title: Create Death Images for Combat Units
tasks.description: Design and create unique death/defeat image assets for each combat unit (Bear, Tiger, Eagle, Goober) that display when units are defeated in battle.
tasks.details:
Create death/defeat image assets for all four combat units with the following specifications:

**Required Assets:**
- bear_death.png - Bear unit defeat image
- tiger_death.png - Tiger unit defeat image  
- eagle_death.png - Eagle unit defeat image
- goober_death.png - Goober unit defeat image

**Visual Design Requirements:**
- Maintain consistency with existing unit art style and color palette
- Use clear visual cues to indicate defeat: dimmed colors, tilted/fallen poses, X-eyes, or similar defeated states
- Ensure images are easily distinguishable from alive unit states
- Maintain same dimensions and resolution as existing unit images
- Consider unit-specific defeat animations: Bear could be lying on side, Tiger sprawled out, Eagle fallen with wings spread, Goober deflated or flattened

**Implementation Considerations:**
- Save images in same format and resolution as existing unit assets
- Follow existing file naming conventions for consistency
- Ensure images work well against various battlefield backgrounds
- Consider adding subtle transparency or overlay effects to enhance the "defeated" appearance
- Test images at different zoom levels to ensure clarity

**File Organization:**
- Place all death images in the same directory as existing unit images
- Update any asset manifest or configuration files to reference new death images
- Document the mapping between unit types and their corresponding death image files
tasks.testStrategy:
Verify task completion through the following steps:

1. **Asset Verification:**
   - Confirm all four death images (bear_death.png, tiger_death.png, eagle_death.png, goober_death.png) are created and properly named
   - Check that image dimensions and file formats match existing unit assets
